leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B035 prize on GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapy, with Drucker and Holst named by every member. The members differ on the third seat: five name Mojsov (el-manira-abdel, linnarsson-sten, perlmann-thomas, sandberg-rickard, svenningsson-per) and one names Knudsen (wahren-herlenius-marie). Citation wording also differs. Five citations centre on physiology and the active peptide form, while the Wahren-Herlenius citation names development into long-acting therapies. No member proposes a second prize part in round 1.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B035 as their preferred prize and describe the physiology-to-therapy chain (proglucagon processing, the active truncated peptide, receptor biology, long-acting agonists) as unusually complete.
All six regard B035 as mature, with independent large outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and none raises a maturity objection to it.
Drucker and Holst are named by all six members as laureates.
All six identify attribution at the third seat as the main weakness, and all note that Habener-type contributions are outside the credited names.
Every member states that no specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted ballots, and none requests recusal.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should be framed around discovery of the hormone and its active form (five members) or should also name the drug-development step (Wahren-Herlenius; several others concede this as the main cost of their own trio).

Whether a strong basic-biology candidate such as the unfolded protein response (B047) is a serious near-term candidate or a later-year one. Members describe its clinical consequence as largely indirect, and no member includes it in a round-1 configuration.
Whether tool-type discoveries (optogenetics, B039) merit a prize ahead of therapies with demonstrated patient benefit. Sandberg explicitly would not support B039 this year.

Whether the commercial and industrial character of the incretin success should weigh in the assessment. Three members (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Wahren-Herlenius) raise it as a concern, and none uses it to oppose B035.
attribution_disputes: B035 has four credited names for three seats. Mojsov (five members) and Knudsen (one member) compete for the third seat after Drucker and Holst.

Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is described as publicly contested, and members say they cannot verify it from the supplied material. Several members state that their account of the incretin history rests on recollection.
Habener-type contributions are outside the credited names, so any B035 trio may be seen as incomplete.

For alternatives, members note gaps outside the credited names: Eshhar and others for CAR-T (B014), upstream cytogenetic and oncogene work and the role of Novartis for BCR-ABL (B011), and a six-name credit split across two steps for optogenetics (B039).
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B035.

Maturity of the alternatives is contested only indirectly. B047 is described as mechanistically original but clinically mostly conceptual, and B039 as a research tool whose clinical record is not yet sufficient.

Svenningsson characterises B047 as less time-urgent than B035, while El-Manira's response records it as ranked fourth. The ranking and its rationale should be read from the member files and not from this summary.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member requests recusal. Each states that no specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted ballots.

Disclosed non-conflicting ties: El-Manira with Perlmann (2009 co-authorship on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons) and with Grillner (2019 review); Perlmann with Svenningsson and El-Manira by co-authorship, with Ronald Evans and with Johan Ericson; Svenningsson with Perlmann (dopamine neuron work); Linnarsson and Sandberg with each other and with Frisen. None involves a credited name on a shortlisted ballot.
Sandberg notes field overlap (RNA processing) with B028 as a field overlap and not a personal tie. El-Manira notes indirect expertise relevance to B039 and B028.
questions_for_round2: Should the third B035 seat go to Mojsov or Knudsen? What evidence on the priority record for the active GLP-1 peptide does each member rely on, and what can be verified from the supplied material and not from recollection?
Should the B035 citation be physiology-led (discovery of GLP-1 and its active form) or also name the drug-development leg? Can one wording be fair to both a Mojsov trio and a Knudsen trio?
How much should the absence of Habener-type contributions from the credited names count against any B035 configuration, and does it change the choice of trio?

Is a second distinct prize part (for example B047, B014, B028 or B011) possible within the three-person cap without cutting a B035 laureate? If not, does any member want B035 alone, or does any member want to restructure B035 to make room for a second part?

If a second part were considered, which alternative is best placed on attribution grounds? Alternatives named so far are B014 (named as an alternative by all six members), B028 (four), B011 (one) and B047 (one), and each has its own credit gaps (Eshhar for B014, upstream work and Novartis for B011).
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 is unanimous on B035 as a single-part prize and on Drucker and Holst, with five of six naming Mojsov and one naming Knudsen as the third laureate. The disagreement is about attribution and framing (discovery versus development) and not about merit or maturity. Alternatives are named only as fallbacks, and no member proposes a two-part configuration. Round 2 should settle the third seat, the citation wording and whether any second part is feasible under the three-person limit.
